hints: The goals in 10 independent matches add up to another Poisson variable. Let $T$ be the total number of goals in the 10 matches and scale the mean $1.36$ for 10 matches.
The supporter pays \$5 per goal, so the amount is $5T$. Use $\text{E}(5T) = 5\,\text{E}(T)$ with the mean of $T$ from your first step.
For any Poisson variable the variance equals the mean. So $\text{Var}(T)$ is the same number as the mean of $T$.
Constants come out of a variance squared: $\text{Var}(5T) = 5^2 \times \text{Var}(T)$. Do not just multiply by 5.
The standard deviation is the square root of the variance you have just found. Give it to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**Name the quantity and find its distribution**

Let $T$ be the total number of goals scored in the next 10 matches. In one match the number of goals is Poisson with mean $1.36$. When you add independent Poisson variables, the result is also Poisson and the means add. So the mean for 10 matches is ten times the mean for one match.

$$\lambda = 10 \times 1.36 = 13.6$$

So $T \sim \text{Po}(13.6)$. This earns the first M1.

**Write the amount paid in terms of $T$**

The supporter gives \$5 for each goal. So the amount paid is $5T$ dollars. We want the expectation and the standard deviation of $5T$.

**Expectation of the amount (A1)**

A Poisson variable has mean equal to its parameter, so $\text{E}(T) = 13.6$. A constant multiplier comes straight out of an expectation.

$$\text{E}(5T) = 5 \times \text{E}(T) = 5 \times 13.6 = 68$$

So the supporter expects to pay \$68.

**Variance of the amount (M1)**

Quick check: for a Poisson variable the variance is equal to the mean, so $\text{Var}(T) = 13.6$ as well.

A constant multiplier comes out of a variance **squared**: $\text{Var}(aT) = a^2\,\text{Var}(T)$. Here $a = 5$.

$$\text{Var}(5T) = 5^2 \times 13.6$$

$$5^2 = 25 \quad\text{and}\quad 25 \times 13.6 = 340$$

Common slip: writing $5 \times 13.6 = 68$ for the variance. That would be correct for the expectation only. This line earns the M1 for $5^2 \times \ldots$ and the next M1 for using the variance of $T$ found above.

**Standard deviation (A1)**

The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.

$$\text{sd} = \sqrt{340}$$

On your calculator type $\sqrt{340}$. It shows $18.439\ldots$ Round to 3 significant figures: the first three digits are $1, 8, 4$ and the next digit is $3$, which is less than 5, so the third digit stays.

$$\text{sd} = 18.4 \text{ (3 s.f.)}$$

The exact form $2\sqrt{85}$ is also accepted, because $340 = 4 \times 85$.

**Final answer**

Expectation of the amount paid: \$68.

Standard deviation of the amount paid: \$18.4 (3 s.f.)
